title: Tenant key routing + sandbox demo — BlueHarbor Logistics
summary: Demo of org/project key patterns, sticky routing, and quota sandboxing tailored to BlueHarbor's multi-tenant routing needs. Focus on burst handling, RBAC, and security integrations. Agreed on a pilot with dedicated project keys + benchmark window.
topics: pilot next steps and benchmark plan

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Chris (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO), Marco (Platform), Leah (InfoSec), Samir (Product)

Summary: quick demo and Q&A on how we recommend keys, quotas, and routing for multi-tenant customers. try to keep it informal — show console and then dive into policy examples.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Monday afternoon. can you hear me okay?
00:05 Priya: Yeah, loud and clear. thanks, Maya.
00:12 Maya: Cool. quick agenda: show the Console org/project key model, then Chris will jump into routing + quota policies, then we can talk security and the pilot shape. sound good?
00:27 Leah: That works. want to make sure we cover audit logs and KMS before we wrap.
00:33 Chris: Yep we'll save a section for KMS and logging.
00:38 Samir: also curious about cost controls — we need to make sure adding redundancy won't explode our bill.

02:02 Maya: Alright opening the Console — forgive the mouse noise — top-left is the organization view. you can see org-level keys that issue project keys, quick note: org keys are for global admin flows, project keys intended for tenant isolation.
02:20 Marco: so project keys are per-tenant? for us that would map to each shipper account?
02:26 Chris: Exactly — you could mint a project key per shipper or per team. that gives you per-key quotas and sticky routing.
02:34 Priya: How does sticky routing actually work if you have multiple regions? we have fleet endpoints in us-east and eu-west.
02:42 Chris: Two layers: routing policy by key + region preference. the Console shows a routing policy where you can say prefer eu-west, fallback to us-east. we also have a sticky token that keeps the same model variant and kernel selection for the session to preserve cache locality — reduces repeated cold KV-cache misses.
02:58 Priya: Got it, so for latency-sensitive flows we pin to a region and route to a cheaper compatible model only on overflow?
03:07 Chris: Yup. the system will prefer the primary region and primary model, but if capacity is constrained it falls back to a compatible quantized variant in a secondary region. you can set those fallbacks per-project key.

05:11 Marco: what's the typical p95 delta when you fall back to quantized models? we can't have more than ~200ms added for our customer chat UIs.
05:23 Chris: In our experience for short contexts (<=512 tokens) quantized LLM variants add about 50–150ms p95 depending on load. longer contexts can see more, obviously. and smart prefix caching reduces tokens that hit the model.
05:36 Marco: ok that seems reasonable.

07:00 Leah: on encryption — we have to ensure keys never leave our boundary; we use AWS KMS with strict key policies. can Redwood integrate?
07:09 Maya: Yes — we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments and in Dedicated via a KMS integration option; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with the ability to bring-your-own-KMS for enterprise tiers.
07:22 Leah: And audit logs? exports? we need immutable retention for 1 year for compliance.
07:28 Chris: Audit logs are exported to your S3 or to our audit endpoint; retention is configurable. for the pilot we can set 12 months retention and provide a read-only dump.

09:10 Maya: pivoting to quotas: Console has quota slicing. here is a sandbox policy where you allocate 10k tokens/day to a project and allow bursts up to 5k tokens within a 10-minute window.
09:26 Samir: so burst window and daily bucket separate — how are they enforced?
09:33 Chris: enforcement is at the routing layer: token counters are tracked per-key with leaky-bucket semantics, plus a short-term sliding window for burst. we also expose per-key metrics so you can tune.
09:43 Priya: can we do concurrency quotas as well? some of our backends fan-out and we want to limit parallel in-flight requests.
09:50 Chris: Yes, concurrency limits per key are supported; you can set hard concurrency ceilings and soft throttles with automatic retry headers.

12:00 Marco: what about a use case: we want priority traffic for enterprise shippers and lower priority for internal dev keys. can we map that?
12:09 Chris: Absolutely — you can assign priorities to project keys and the router will do capacity weight shares. config shows a priority lane that takes 70% of capacity for enterprise keys, 20% for standard, 10% for dev.
12:22 Marco: and billing attaches to org or project keys?
12:26 Maya: Billing can be by org with project-level tagging; we emit usage records per-key so you can attribute in your billing system.

14:00 Leah: security question — how do you handle key rotation? we need automatic rotation and the ability to revoke a key immediately.
14:09 Chris: Keys can be rotated via API or Console; revocation is immediate and you can set grace windows for long-running sessions. we also support short-lived ephemeral keys for internal microservices.

16:30 Maya: quick demo of a policy JSON snippet — apologies if the transcription mangles code. here's a sample:
16:40 Chris: "policy": "{ 'key_type': 'project', 'daily_tokens': 10000, 'burst_tokens': 5000, 'burst_window_sec': 600, 'priority': 'enterprise', 'fallback_models': ['gpt-q-8bit','gpt-compat']}"
16:56 Marco: looks good. can we template those policies so our infra team can generate them on onboarding?
17:03 Chris: Yes we support templated policies and an API to bulk-mint keys with pre-applied policies. many customers wire that into provisioning pipelines.

19:20 Priya: On observability, will we get token-level traces? our SREs want to see which prompt caused high cost.
19:28 Chris: We provide token-level cost breakdowns, per-request latency spikes, model decision traces, and prefix cache hit rates. Sensitive content is redacted on request.

21:05 Samir: about sandboxing — we want a staging tenant that can mimic production cost to validate prompts. how does that look?
21:13 Maya: We usually do a dedicated sandbox project with mirrored quotas and throttles but using cheaper model variants for cost control; you can replay real traces into it.
21:23 Marco: replay — do you accept our trace format? we have a compact shape with timestamp, prompt size, tokens.
21:30 Chris: we accept JSONL and can ingest CSV via a small adapter. we'll add that to the benchmark playbook.

24:00 Leah: any PCI / HIPAA specifics? we process shipping manifests with some PHI.
24:10 Maya: For PHI, Private deployments or Dedicated with hardened networking is recommended. we do have HIPAA BAAs for certain tiers; our security docs detail controls. we'll include HIPAA specifics in the pack.

26:45 Marco: let's talk about failure modes — if a region fully saturates and fallback can't keep up, what happens to the request? do we drop it or queue?
26:55 Chris: We have several strategies: queue with a short backpressure window, degrade to a cheaper model (if acceptable), or return a 429 with a suggested retry-after. you can configure fallback order and preferred behavior per key.
27:10 Marco: what about backpressure signals to our edge? can we propagate Retry-After headers upstream?
27:17 Chris: yes we include standard Retry-After and a custom x-rdwd-backpressure header with reason codes. you can map those in your gateway to circuit breakers.

30:00 Maya: price sensitivity note: Samir mentioned costs earlier — our Optimize module can run a per-workload quantization suggestion and batching configs to hit a cost target while staying within SLOs.
30:13 Samir: Is that automated? we don't want manual tuning forever.
30:18 Chris: It's a mix: Optimize suggests profiles and can run A/B tests. you can set a cost target and it will propose profiles and simulate impact. actual rollout is under your control.

33:00 Priya: For the pilot, we want three things measured: p95 latency for 512 tokens, cost per 1k tokens, and cache hit rates. can Redwood show those in Console?
33:10 Chris: Yes — Dashboard templates exist. we'll also push a dashboard to your tenant for the pilot so you can watch live metrics.

35:00 Marco: timeline question — how fast can you stand up a pilot with dedicated project keys and a small traffic mirror?
35:09 Maya: We can spin up a pilot in 5–7 business days once we've exchanged security paperwork and got sample traces. provisioning time depends on whether you choose Hosted Dedicated or Private.
35:20 Priya: We probably want Dedicated for predictable throughput.
35:24 Maya: That makes sense for BlueHarbor's SLAs.

37:50 Leah: one more on compliance — do you support SAML-based SSO and fine-grained RBAC? we need separate admin/ops/readonly roles.
37:58 Chris: Yes SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based permissions. you can also scope RBAC to projects.

40:00 Samir: any gotchas we should know about when migrating existing usage?
40:07 Chris: Biggest one is key granularity — if you under-shard keys you'll lose attribution and can't isolate noisy tenants. also be mindful of prompt design because caching helps only if prefixes are stable. we'll help craft a keying strategy during onboarding.

42:15 Maya: quick run through next steps: we'll send security docs, propose pilot dates, Chris will draft the benchmark plan, and Marco will confirm networking.

44:30 Priya: ok sounds good. one small ask: can we get an estimate of cost delta if we run an always-on small model for dev vs routing to hosted?
44:40 Chris: We'll include cost scenarios in the spreadsheet; quick ballpark: dev always-on small model likely 2–3x cheaper than dev routing to full model because of resource sharing, but exact numbers depend on concurrency.

46:50 Maya: cool. any final questions?
46:55 Marco: none from me.
47:02 Leah: just please include the retention detail for logs, we need explicit config steps.
47:07 Maya: will do.
47:15 Priya: let's tentatively plan pilot start week of May 11, pending docs.

50:00 Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the pack and scheduling links.
50:06 Samir: great, thanks.
50:12 Priya: thanks all.
50:20 (call ends)
